briefs.label: Small winged hatchling (scale tuned to speed)
briefs.why: A small winged lizard with a clear speed budget: the comment says a hatchling this small cannot foot-match a fast chase, so the donor keeps a small slide and tunes scale to walk and run speeds. The silhouette is a small body with wings that reads as a pest, not a threat.
keep: scale tuned to walk and run speed (walk 0.54, run 1.87 at scale 0.85)
a per-creature clip set rather than a shared one
change: a horn crest and tail fin in our palette, not the donor's
a flap-hop locomotion instead of a walk
a clip set that is not shared with the bigger dragon family

a snap ability with a visible sound beat instead of a plain swipe

lower rate for a heavier blow
sound fired on the same frame as the sim blow
change: our own telegraph sound, not re-pitched forge samples
a rising tone before the drop
no reuse of the donor's sample keys

inspiration: Procedural first, curated second: README line 56 says the scene is authored in code, not a 3D editor, and only the models that ship are curated. Keeps phone download size low.

Rigged families with a full set of animations: README line 347 says rigged creature families carry walk, attack, cast, sit and death. Family-level animation sets with hit-variety bundles per family (public/models/chars/enemies/*_hit_variety_anims.glb).

Boss telegraph sound as a beat table: hoard_mechanic_audio_core.ts (lines 1-5) plays each mechanic's sound at the moment its blow lands, using gain and playback rate for weight. Best sound-cue idea in this donor; matches our row 12 cues.

One music layer per location by priority: musicZoneForLocation (music_zones.ts lines 122-134) takes dungeon first, then hub, then zone, then biome. Music changes on dungeon entry only when the dungeon id changes (shouldResetMusicForDungeonEntry, lines 114-118).

Speed-tuned creature scale: a comment (manifest.ts lines 3149-3151) explains the scale and speed trade-off for a small creature. Useful as a rule to write down for each creature in our catalogue (row 21).
Catalogue as runtime source: 101 mob_ entries in one manifest, each with url, height, clips and notes (manifest.ts line 3144 onward). Matches our catalogue-as-runtime row 20.
Collision as data per prop: thornhollow_assets.json lists boxes and ramps per prop with an overrideMode field, so the collision shape is data, not the mesh. Good for arena obstacles.

Readable hazard telegraphs by sound and shape: boss mechanics (hammer, boulder, tentacles, cocoon) each have a named prop and a sound table (CREDITS.md lines 447-487). Category idea only; instance names are not ours to use.
